citation.authors: Broussard JL, Kilkus JM, Delebecque F, Abraham V, Day A, Whitmore HR, Tasali E
citation.title: Elevated ghrelin predicts food intake during experimental sleep restriction

reported.what: 24-hour mean ghrelin, normal sleep against sleep restriction, mean ± SEM, n=19 (Table 1); the profile follows several days of standardized meals whose grams are not printed

location.where: Table 1, Ghrelin, 24-hour mean (pg/mL) row, Normal Sleep and Sleep Restriction columns

reported.what: 24-hour mean leptin, normal sleep against sleep restriction, mean ± SEM, n=19 (Table 1); same meal gap

location.where: Table 1, Leptin, 24-hour mean (ng/mL) row, Normal Sleep and Sleep Restriction columns

reported.what: percent body fat by bioimpedance at admission, before each sleep condition, mean ± SEM, n=19; the model carries fat mass in kg, not a percentage, and the body weight needed to convert it is averaged over four days

location.where: Results, Body weight and percent body fat

detail: The Table 1 profiles follow several days of standardized meals (three a day at 09:00, 14:00 and 19:00, plus a 19:00 meal before sampling) that the paper gives only as percentages of energy, with the energy itself (Schofield equation) not printed, so no meal can be written in grams; that gap alone blocks the leptin means, and absolute ghrelin levels would be left out under the guide's total-versus-active rule in any case.
